messages:
Maya K.: ran a quick sweep across regions comparing continuous-batcher behavior with different batch_window_ms and max_batch_tokens. posting raw observations.

Liam R.: nice — what models / GPUs?

Maya K.: mosaic-13b q2b on h100 (us-west), a100 (eu-west), and gpusim (apac env). default scheduler + fairness turned on.

Sophia T.: curious about fairness config — did you use priority queues for real-time vs background?

Maya K.: yes. two priority classes: interactive (priority=10) and background (priority=1). baseline: priority is strict FIFO within class.

Maya K.: short summary:
- h100 (us-west): highest throughput but tail latency spikes for background when interactive load bursts > 60 qps
- a100 (eu-west): lower peak throughput, smoother tail under same config
- apac (gpusim): synthetic, shows scheduler degenerates if batch_window_ms > 25ms for short sequences

Liam R.: do you have numbers?

Maya K.: pasted a tiny csv here for the important rows:

```
region,gpu,batch_window_ms,max_batch_tokens,interactive_p50,interactive_p95,background_p95,throughput_tok/s
us-west,h100,10,1024,12ms,28ms,220ms,145000
us-west,h100,40,4096,20ms,45ms,840ms,178000
eu-west,a100,10,1024,15ms,36ms,120ms,98000
eu-west,a100,40,4096,22ms,58ms,360ms,120000
apac,gpusim,60,2048,18ms,55ms,560ms,62000
```

Maya K.: key signal: increasing batch_window_ms and max_batch_tokens helps throughput but background fairness collapses on h100 under bursty interactive traffic — background p95 jumps 4x.

Sophia T.: could be due to KV-cache eviction timing + kernel selection causing long running tokens to block queue. did bench-bot log kernel durations?

bench-bot: kernel_log: avg_forward_kernel_ms: {h100: 0.9, a100: 1.3}, long_tail_percentile_ops detected: 0.7% on h100 during high-batch runs.

Maya K.: I instrumented scheduler: problem is continuous-batcher coalescing multiple interactive requests into one giant batch; priority queue drains but background batches starve because we prefer filling to max_batch_tokens.

Liam R.: two quick mitigations to try: 1) priority_decay (reduce effective priority of interactive requests after X ms waiting) 2) max_headroom_for_background (reserve a token budget per batch for low-priority).

Maya K.: tried both in a short run: priority_decay=0.5 after 30ms and reserve_tokens=512. results: background_p95 down to ~180ms on h100 with batch_window_ms=40. throughput token/s only -3%.

Sophia T.: nice. can you paste the updated csv row?

Maya K.: updated rows:
```
us-west,h100,40,4096,priority_decay=0.5,reserve_tokens=512,interactive_p95=48ms,background_p95=190ms,throughput_tok/s=172000
```

Liam R.: sounds promising. did you test regional kernel selection differences? maybe h100 picks fused kernel that increases per-batch setup cost?

Maya K.: yes, kernel profiler shows h100 path picks an optimized fused attention kernel for >2048 tokens which increases per-batch prep by ~6ms; that amplification matters when coalesced batches are heterogeneous. a100 tends to stay on smaller-kernel path.

Sophia T.: action items:
- run an exhaustive grid across batch_window_ms [10,25,40,60], max_batch_tokens [1024,2048,4096], reserve_tokens [0,256,512] in us-west and eu-west.
- add priority_decay knobs and measure background_p95 and tail fairness metric (background_p95 / interactive_p95).
- capture kernel selection tag per request for correlation.

Maya K.: I'll start the grid tomorrow and post aggregated charts. planning to use bench-bot to dump per-request kernel_tag and batch_size.

ops-bot: scheduled job: continuous-batcher-grid-us-west-eu-1765543210 queued. ETA ~3h.

Liam R.: if we can automate a follow-up that suggests reserve_tokens per GPU type (h100 higher reserve since fused kernels amplify starvation), that'd be great.

Sophia T.: agree. also add a small eval for quality regressions when we change max_batch_tokens (prompt truncation interactions).

Maya K.: noted — will include a small eval set (100 prompts) to verify generation parity.

Liam R.: thanks — ping me if a run shows surprising kernel/tag combos. :thumbsup:

Sophia T.: :eyes:

Maya K.: will update with charts + a short thread summary once done.
